method: Original summaries verified against publisher, author, academic and exact-edition catalogue evidence. ISBN, title, author and language guard every text. Facts shared by a work are distinguished from edition-specific claims. No generic withdrawn-provider fallback is enabled.

entries.title: Against the Grain
entries.author: James C. Scott
entries.text: James C. Scott questions the familiar idea that farming naturally led people towards safer, more prosperous lives under the earliest states. Drawing on archaeology and history, he examines grain cultivation, domestication, disease and the control of labour. Settled agriculture appears alongside alternatives pursued by people who remained outside state authority. This study of early political organisation asks who benefited from those changes and what their costs were, connecting the material conditions of food production with the growth of power.
entries.identityNotes: Exact hardcover ISBN confirmed in OL26934620M; Yale paperback page supplies the shared work synopsis.

entries.title: The Romanovs
entries.author: Simon Sebag-Montefiore
entries.text: Simon Sebag Montefiore follows the Romanov dynasty through three centuries of Russian rule, from 1613 to 1918. His account connects the ambitions of individual tsars and tsarinas with the expansion and eventual collapse of their empire. Court intrigue, family rivalry and the exercise of autocratic power shape the narrative. Drawing on archival research, the book moves between rulers' private lives and the wider consequences of their decisions, treating the dynasty as both a family history and a study of political power.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Knopf hardcover ISBN and subtitle 1613–1918 confirmed in OL27210242M; source describes the same history.

entries.title: Nineteen Minutes
entries.author: Jodi Picoult
entries.text: A school shooting leaves the town of Sterling grieving and searching for answers. Peter Houghton, who has endured years of bullying, is brought to trial for the killings. As the case develops, the testimony exposes relationships and choices that complicate the community's understanding of what happened. Jodi Picoult follows the aftermath of the violence through a story about responsibility, exclusion and justice, asking how a town confronts both a crime and the circumstances surrounding the person who committed it.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher page and catalogue record confirm the exact selected ISBN.

entries.title: Les Miserables
entries.author: Victor Hugo
entries.text: Jean Valjean tries to build a new life after imprisonment for stealing bread, but his past continues to follow him. His encounters with Fantine, her daughter Cosette and the determined inspector Javert connect personal struggles with the injustices of nineteenth-century France. Victor Hugo's novel moves through poverty, love, political unrest and the possibility of redemption. Its story reaches from provincial life to the streets and barricades of Paris, exploring the distance between legal punishment and human compassion.
entries.identityNotes: Selected Amereon edition ISBN confirmed in OL8258182M. Only shared novel facts used; no claim that this is the Julie Rose translation or Modern Library edition.

entries.title: Secrets of The lost symbol
entries.author: John Michael Greer
entries.text: John Michael Greer examines the secret societies, symbols and occult traditions that appear in Dan Brown's The Lost Symbol. Organised as a reference guide, the book provides background for readers who want to distinguish the novel's inventions from the histories and ideas it draws upon. Its entries introduce mystical concepts and organisations rather than continuing Robert Langdon's fictional adventure. This is an unauthorised companion to Brown's novel, with an emphasis on explaining the material behind its puzzles and references.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN, author and subtitle confirmed in OL24033307M. Publisher article confirms encyclopedic format and relationship to the novel.

entries.title: Surviving Hitler
entries.author: Andrea Warren
entries.text: Andrea Warren tells the story of Jack Mandelbaum, a Polish Jewish boy whose adolescence was shaped by Nazi occupation and imprisonment. Drawing on his recollections, she follows the separation from his family, his struggle to survive the camps and the life he built after liberation. Written for younger readers, this nonfiction account connects one person's experiences with the history of the Holocaust. Jack's wish to survive and find his family gives the book its personal focus amid a much wider catastrophe.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Paw Prints edition confirmed in OL37853755M; original HarperCollins publication and author synopsis agree.

entries.title: Dust Bowl
entries.author: Donald Worster
entries.text: Donald Worster examines the southern Great Plains during the Dust Bowl of the 1930s. The book brings the experiences of two affected communities into a history of farming, dust storms and economic hardship. Personal recollections give the regional account a local perspective, connecting environmental disaster with the lives of people who endured it. Published by Oxford University Press, this historical study focuses on a particular landscape and period within the broader upheaval of the Great Depression.
entries.identityNotes: FAO/National Agricultural Library record explicitly includes exact ISBN 9780195032123 and the two-community account; OL7386171M independently confirms the selected edition.

entries.title: Out of Darkness
entries.author: Ashley Hope Pérez
entries.text: In New London, Texas, in 1937, Naomi Vargas and Wash Fuller find themselves drawn to one another across the racial divisions of their town. Naomi is Mexican American and Wash is Black; the hostility around them makes their relationship dangerous. Ashley Hope Pérez places this young adult historical novel against the background of the New London school explosion. The story explores love, family and prejudice while bringing attention to people whose lives are often left out of accounts of the period.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Holiday House paperback ISBN confirmed on publisher and catalogue pages.

entries.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
entries.author: J. K. Rowling
entries.sourceName: J. K. Rowling — official author site
entries.text: Harry Potter wants to return to Hogwarts for his second year, despite warnings from a house-elf named Dobby. Back at school, unsettling voices in the corridors are followed by attacks that leave students seemingly turned to stone. The mystery makes Dobby's warning increasingly difficult to dismiss. This second book in the series follows Harry and his friends as familiar school routines give way to suspicion and danger, with the secrets of Hogwarts becoming central to the threat around them.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Scholastic edition ISBN 9780439064866 and series year 2 confirmed in OL383855M.

entries.title: Beware!
entries.author: Robert Lawrence Stine
entries.text: R. L. Stine brings together a selection of frightening stories and poems, adding two tales of his own. The collection includes Bram Stoker's The Judge's House and Ray Bradbury's The Black Ferris, alongside verse by Shel Silverstein and Jack Prelutsky. Its mix of suspense, strange encounters and humour offers several kinds of short scary reading in one volume. Stine is the selector as well as a contributor: this anthology contains work by multiple writers rather than a single continuing story.
entries.identityNotes: Exact hardcover 9780066238425 is OL7293417M; Google Books gives contents for the same anthology in paperback 9780060555474. No edition-specific page count copied.

entries.title: Een spoor van vernieling
entries.author: Tim Weiner
entries.sourceName: Penguin Random House — Legacy of Ashes
entries.text: Tim Weiner onderzoekt de geschiedenis van de CIA en de gevolgen van haar geheime operaties. Hij richt zich op de verhouding tussen de ambities van de Amerikaanse inlichtingendienst en de resultaten van haar werk. Fouten, bestuurlijke keuzes en nationale veiligheid vormen de kern van zijn kritische geschiedschrijving. Een spoor van vernieling is de Nederlandse vertaling van Legacy of Ashes. Het boek biedt daarmee een journalistieke ingang tot de rol van de CIA in het Amerikaanse buitenlandse beleid.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Dutch edition, translators and English work association confirmed in OL33221115M and Dutch publisher author biography. Publisher evidence for the original work is not represented as a Dutch edition.

entries.title: De gentleman-bandiet
entries.author: Marije Plomp
entries.text: Marije Plomp brengt levensverhalen en literatuur over Nederlands-Indië en Indonesië bijeen, met de jaren 1930–1960 als afgebakende periode. Persoonlijke herinneringen staan naast beschouwingen over verhalen uit en over die tijd. Zo verbindt de bundel individuele ervaringen met de manier waarop een ingrijpend veranderende samenleving wordt beschreven. De combinatie van geschiedenis en literatuur biedt verschillende ingangen tot het koloniale verleden, de oorlogsjaren en de overgang naar onafhankelijkheid.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Boom edition confirmed in OL22674735M. Brill contributor biography explicitly describes this as a collection of life stories and essays on literature; DW B independently discusses interviews alongside literary fragments.

entries.title: A Swim in a Pond in the Rain
entries.author: George Saunders
entries.text: George Saunders invites readers into the close study of seven Russian short stories, pairing the fiction with essays about how it works. Chekhov, Turgenev, Tolstoy and Gogol provide the examples for discussions of structure, attention and the choices that keep a reader involved. Drawing on his teaching, Saunders treats reading and writing as connected practices. This is a book of literary exploration and practical observation, intended for people curious about stories as well as those trying to write them.
entries.identityNotes: Exact hardcover 9781984856029 confirmed in OL28719190M, including contents. Current publisher paperback page supplies shared work facts.

entries.title: The Summer I Died
entries.author: Ryan C. Thomas
entries.sourceName: Ryan C. Thomas — official author site
entries.text: Roger Huntington returns from college expecting an ordinary summer with his friend Tooth. A trip to Bobcat Mountain turns that reunion into a fight for survival when the two encounter a sadistic killer. Their friendship and their ideas about courage are tested as the situation becomes increasingly violent. Ryan C. Thomas begins the Roger Huntington saga with this survival horror novel, replacing the prospect of a carefree holiday with an intense account of captivity, fear and desperate choices.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Necro Publications edition confirmed in OL8727073M; author site supplies synopsis and first-in-series relationship.

entries.title: Charlie Hernández and the League of Shadows
entries.author: Ryan Calejo
entries.text: Charlie Hernández has grown up hearing his grandmother's stories about the creatures of Hispanic folklore. When strange changes begin happening to his own body, those familiar legends become part of an urgent mystery. With Violet Rey beside him, Charlie enters a conflict between supernatural forces while trying to understand himself and find his missing parents. This opening adventure in Ryan Calejo's series draws on traditions from the Iberian Peninsula and Latin America, combining a young hero's search with mythological danger.
entries.identityNotes: Selected ebook ISBN 9781534426603 confirmed in OL34076482M; publisher page is the same first-series work in paperback.

entries.title: Life expectancy
entries.author: Dean Koontz
entries.text: On the night Jimmy Tock is born, his dying grandfather predicts five dates when terrible events will threaten the boy's future. Other accurate details in the prediction make it difficult for the family to dismiss his warning. As Jimmy grows older, those approaching days shape a story of danger, unexpected encounters and the struggle to face an uncertain fate. Dean Koontz follows the five crises across Jimmy's life, combining suspense with questions about courage and the forces of good and evil.
entries.identityNotes: Exact selected English edition confirmed in OL35335892M; author provides the full work synopsis.

entries.title: LAST WATCH (Night Watch)
entries.author: Sergeĭ Lukʹi͡anenko
entries.text: The death of a Russian tourist in Edinburgh appears to be the work of a rogue vampire. Anton is sent to investigate, but the case leads beyond a single killing to a search for a magical treasure associated with Merlin. In this fourth Night Watch novel, the supernatural Others and their rival allegiances to Light and Dark return. The investigation draws Anton further into the mysteries of the Twilight, where the consequences of the treasure hunt reach beyond the original crime.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Hyperion edition ISBN confirmed in OL11591039M. Penguin confirms the same fourth Night Watch novel; unrelated Pratchett book must not be confused with this series.

entries.title: Gent, Rabot
entries.author: Bart de Wilde
entries.text: Bart De Wilde beschrijft de geschiedenis van de Gentse Rabotwijk vanuit de opkomst en teloorgang van de textielnijverheid. De fabrieken bepaalden niet alleen het werk, maar ook het wonen en sociale leven in de buurt. Historisch onderzoek, documenten en herinneringen van bewoners brengen die samenhang in beeld. De geïllustreerde uitgave volgt vervolgens de veranderingen die het verdwijnen van de industrie voor de wijk en haar bewoners betekende.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN and project Memory On-Off confirmed in Amsab-ISG catalogue. Content scope, residents documents and oral accounts independently verified in the University of Ghent journal review.

entries.title: Too Late to Say Goodbye
entries.author: Ann Rule
entries.text: Ann Rule investigates the deaths of Jenn Corbin and Dorothy Hearn, two women connected to the same man and initially believed to have taken their own lives. As investigators examine the circumstances, events separated by fourteen years begin to form a different picture. Drawing on interviews with relatives, detectives and others involved, Rule reconstructs the case and the relationships behind it. This true-crime account follows the work of establishing what happened beneath the appearance of a successful, settled life.
entries.identityNotes: Exact large-print edition ISBN confirmed in OL8893004M; publisher synopsis is used only for the common nonfiction work, without details unique to a later edition.

entries.title: Lily the Lost Puppy (Puppy Friends)
entries.author: Jenny Dale
entries.text: Lily's family is preparing to move, and Jack has told his puppy about their new home. During the move, however, Lily is accidentally left behind. Her adventure centres on the separation from the boy she knows and the hope of finding her family again. This short illustrated story is part of Jenny Dale's Puppy Friends series, which gives individual puppies their own adventures. Here the familiar upheaval of moving house becomes a small animal's search for the people who belong with her.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN 9780689834042, publisher, illustrator and series volume 2 confirmed in Google Books and OL7729435M.
